pricing.freeTierCaps: 100 tasks/month, 2-step Zaps, 1 seat, 15-minute polling, 2,500 table records/account, 3 views/table, 10 form pages and 5 MB maximum form upload
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual prices are effective monthly rates and plans scale by task volume
pricing.hiddenCosts: Pay-per-task overage is enabled by default on eligible paid plans. Some newer units cost multiple tasks: MCP calls use 2, Lead Router steps 5, AI actions can use 1/3/5 by model tier, and extended code uses 1 task per 30 seconds. Agents and Chatbots are separate products or add-ons.

verdictSummary: A few personal automations are easy; Zapier's moat is the 9,000+ app integration catalog, auth handling, retries, task history, UI, and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Write scripts or an n8n/Activepieces flow to call the handful of APIs you actually need.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because every new app connection is already packaged and maintained.

priorArt.name: n8n
priorArt.desc: Open-source workflow automation platform and a real Zapier alternative for technical users

alternatives.name: Activepieces Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Zapier with a Docker bill and no task meter.

facts.install: Hosted signup, single-container Docker for testing, or Docker Compose for production
facts.engines: AI pieces connect to providers including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini
facts.dataFormat: Flows and credentials in PostgreSQL; queues and cache in Redis; files use configured persistent or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its connector catalog, edge-case handling, documentation and vendor support are smaller than Zapier's, and self-hosted OAuth connections can be fiddly.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, a public URL and OAuth credentials for many connectors

alternatives.name: Automatisch
alternatives.desc: A smaller AGPL Zapier clone for ordinary trigger-action flows.

facts.dataFormat: Automation definitions and credentials in PostgreSQL; jobs and cache in Redis on the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: It has a far smaller integration catalog and less mature debugging, administration and support than Zapier.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker plus PostgreSQL, Redis and a public OAuth callback URL for many app connections

alternatives.name: n8n Community Edition
alternatives.desc: The standard self-hosted answer: broad, durable, and fair-code rather than open source.

facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and many hosted or open-model providers through AI nodes and LangChain integrations
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosting defaults to SQLite in the persistent .n8n directory; PostgreSQL is supported, credentials are encrypted in the database, and binary files use filesystem or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is more technical to build and debug, and self-hosting moves reliability and upgrades onto you while Zapier offers a larger turnkey app ecosystem.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs persistent storage, a public webhook URL, credentials and operations; the Sustainable Use License is source-available rather than OSI open source

notes: A structural kinda: one automation yes, Zapier the integration network no.
prompt:
Build me a personal automation runner to replace Zapier, for the handful of pipelines I actually use. Requirements:

- One Node process on my VPS: Express for incoming webhooks, node-cron for
  schedules. A pipeline is a plain JS file in pipelines/ exporting a trigger (cron
  expression or webhook path) and an async run(payload).
- Steps are just code: fetch() calls to the APIs I need, every key in .env. Adding
  an integration means writing 20 lines, not finding a connector.
- Every run logged to SQLite (better-sqlite3): pipeline, trigger payload, status,
  duration, error. Failures retry 3 times with exponential backoff via p-retry.
- A /runs page (bound to localhost) showing the last 100 runs with status and an
  expandable payload/error view, plus a re-run button.
- After the final failed retry, notify me via an ntfy topic in .env.
- Webhook URLs include a per-pipeline secret token; reject anything else.
- Ship two example pipelines: a cron one (daily 08:00, fetch a weather API, push
  to ntfy) and a webhook one (POST in, append a row to a CSV).
- No accounts, no telemetry, no visual editor.
- Out of scope: OAuth flows for third-party apps (token-based APIs only) and any
  connector catalog. A service that only offers OAuth will cost an afternoon each,
  say so in the README.
- README: systemd unit, how to add a pipeline, .env layout.
